extension_description.message: Keep AWS console sessions separated in Firefox containers and organize their tabs by account.

locale_code.description: Language code for this catalog. Translate to the target language code.

locale_direction.description: Text direction for this catalog: ltr or rtl.

ui_choosing_a_method_only_selects_its_se.message: Choosing a method only selects its setup panel. Firefox asks for site access later, when you use that panel's explicit setup button.

ui_choose_how_containoodle_opens_aws_con.message: Choose how Containoodle opens AWS console sessions

ui_use_value_with_an_existing_aws_cli_ss.message: Use $value1$ with an existing AWS CLI SSO login when the access portal is unavailable.
ui_use_value_with_an_existing_aws_cli_ss.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (server.py). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_choose_an_account_and_role_in_the_por.message: Choose an account and role in the portal; Containoodle moves that console launch into its isolated container.

ui_containoodle_gets_accounts_and_sign_i.message: Containoodle gets accounts and sign-in URLs from the helper running on this computer.

ui_the_url_token_and_profile_are_replace.message: The URL, token, and profile are replaced only after a successful test, which also refreshes the account list.

ui_run_value_to_print_the_helper_s_persi.message: Run $value1$ to print the helper's persistent 43-character token. That command then exits, so start $value2$ separately. Paste the token here once; it is stored only in this Firefox profile and never redisplayed after saving. Leave this field blank to test with the token already stored.
ui_run_value_to_print_the_helper_s_persi.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (python3 server.py --show-token). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $2 is code (python3 server.py). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_optional_enter_the_local_profile_alia.message: Optional. Enter the local profile alias used with $value1$. Leave it blank only when the helper can identify one valid SSO login.
ui_optional_enter_the_local_profile_alia.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (aws sso login --profile …). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_the_helper_refreshes_this_browser_cac.message: The helper refreshes this browser cache from $value1$; edit the source file to change backend accounts.
ui_the_helper_refreshes_this_browser_cac.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (~/.aws/accounts.json). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_offered_during_your_first_helper_setu.message: Offered during your first helper setup

ui_when_enabled_containoodle_can_check_w.message: When enabled, Containoodle can check whether this account's container is already signed in and reuse that session instead of starting another sign-in. It also suppresses the AWS cookie banner in new containers.

ui_on_your_first_local_helper_value_fire.message: On your first local-helper $value1$, Firefox asks once for access limited to $value2$. Accepting enables session reuse; declining does not block setup or normal backend launches. Containoodle will not ask automatically again, but you can use $value3$ below. Revoking access stops future checks but does not delete cookies already managed by Firefox.
ui_on_your_first_local_helper_value_fire.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is strong (Save & test). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $2 is code (*.console.aws.amazon.com). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $3 is strong (Allow session reuse). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_an_older_broad_aws_grant_keeps_workin.message: An older broad AWS grant keeps working until you explicitly tighten or revoke it. If Firefox says the broad grant still covers a narrower request, use $value1$, then $value2$ again. Opening Options, updating Containoodle, and switching modes do not migrate existing permissions.
ui_an_older_broad_aws_grant_keeps_workin.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is strong (Revoke). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $2 is strong (Allow session reuse). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_sign_in_normally_then_choose_an_accou.message: Sign in normally, then choose an account and role. No local helper or AWS CLI is required.

ui_firefox_will_ask_for_access_only_to_t.message: Firefox will ask for access only to this exact portal origin. Optional role choices for favorite sidebar accounts are managed separately below.

ui_containoodle_needs_permission_for_thi.message: Containoodle needs permission for this portal and a signed-in portal session before it can hand off a launch.

ui_keep_portal_accounts_as_direct_launch.message: Keep portal accounts as direct-launch shortcuts

ui_open_an_account_from_the_aws_access_p.message: Open an account from the AWS access portal, then choose ☆ on its active row in the Containoodle sidebar. It changes to ★ and keeps the account as a direct-launch shortcut after its tabs are closed. Choosing ★ again removes only the shortcut.

ui_pinned_accounts_belong_only_to_portal.message: These favorites belong only to portal mode. Helper-mode favorites are saved separately from accounts supplied by the local helper.

ui_allow_this_only_if_you_want_containoo.message: Allow this only if you want Containoodle to ask the AWS access portal which roles you can choose when launching or changing a favorite. Firefox asks only for the detected regional $value1$ endpoint. Saving favorites and normal portal clicks work without it.
ui_allow_this_only_if_you_want_containoo.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (portal.sso.<region>.amazonaws.com). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_an_older_broad_aws_api_grant_keeps_wo.message: An older broad AWS API grant keeps working until you explicitly tighten or revoke it. If Firefox keeps only the broad grant after a narrower request, use $value1$, then $value2$ again. Opening Options, updating Containoodle, and switching modes do not migrate existing permissions.
ui_an_older_broad_aws_api_grant_keeps_wo.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is strong (Revoke). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $2 is strong (Allow role choices). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_use_only_when_automatic_role_lookup_c.message: Use only when automatic role lookup cannot detect it

ui_this_affects_only_role_lookup_for_pin.message: This affects only role lookup for favorites. Leave it blank unless automatic detection fails.

ui_containoodle_copies_your_portal_sessi.message: Containoodle copies your portal session cookie into the selected account container and verifies the copy before navigation. Optional sidebar role discovery sends that value directly to the AWS portal API. The value is never stored in extension storage or logged.

ui_on_the_configured_portal_page_contain.message: On the configured portal page, Containoodle reads the URL and displayed account name belonging to the console shortcut you click. It does not read forms, credentials, or the rest of the account list. Configuration stays in this Firefox profile.

ui_use_one_javascript_regular_expression.message: Use one JavaScript regular expression for sidebar account labels, automatic container names, and automatic tab-group titles. It applies to all helper accounts and to open or favorite portal accounts.

ui_enter_the_pattern_without_value_delim.message: Enter the pattern without $value1$ delimiters. Leave it empty—or let it not match—to keep the original account name. Backtracking-prone constructs are rejected.
ui_enter_the_pattern_without_value_delim.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code (/…/). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_use_value_value_or_named_captures_suc.message: Use $value1$, $value2$, or named captures such as $value3$. An empty or overlong result falls back to the original name.
ui_use_value_value_or_named_captures_suc.description: Interface text. Existing markup slots: $1 is code ($1). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $2 is code ($2). Keep each placeholder exactly once. $3 is code ($<name>). Keep each placeholder exactly once.

ui_saving_updates_sidebar_labels_and_aut.message: Saving updates sidebar labels and automatic container and tab-group names. Original account data, account IDs, sessions, and environment colours are unchanged. Manually renamed containers and tab groups keep their custom names. Resetting clears only tab-group title overrides and recalculates those titles from the saved rule; custom container names are not reset.
